rows.evidence: The if at src/core/agent-runtime/session-operations.ts:470 is reached only in the `from === frozenUpper` terminal-page branch (:460). A cheaper check would be wrong: with a platform-issued cursor the frozen upper is a position the platform already read (:411-418 for range, :424-448 for the cursor), and the Kernel log only grows: vendor/coding-agent/dist/storage/adapters/sqlite/sqlite-stores.js:397 has the only session_records write (INSERT), :439-445 computes lastPosition as MAX(position), and neither src nor vendor/coding-agent/dist contains a DELETE/UPDATE of session_records (checked grep). Each read opens the store afresh (src/core/agent-runtime/kernel-store-locator.ts:107-111), so a committed record cannot be rolled back into a shorter tail either. The only writer that can shrink the tail is a foreign one: a hand-edited/restored Kernel DB. Before T the only test that executed this arm did exactly that: .dsh-ref/before/tests/runtime/R4c-graph-history.test.ts:867 reaches the empty terminal page, then DatabaseSync DELETE (:897-904) and expects unavailable, which is TP-112 (.dsh-ref/evidence/books/t-items-TP.md:822-824, tamper). After T that block is gone (tests/runtime/R4c-graph-history.test.ts:867-895 keeps only the legal empty page) and grep finds no after-T test at all for the message at :471; the range-past-tail test (:849-853) covers only the sibling check at :494-495. One caveat, not a refutation: the kernhist1 cursor is unsigned base64 JSON (:170-223) and a caller who rebuilds it with i = u > real tail reaches :470 through the plain sessions/history route (src/app/core-routes.ts:400, :1079 -> src/composition/create-platform.ts:1463-1464) with no store edit. That is hand-made platform-issued input, not a public step (test-rule-sheet-v2.md:33 allows a cursor only as a real step returned it), and it is still foreign input in a shape no platform writer produces, so U, not G.
rows.proposal_note: Keep the guard untested; both proposals do. It is inline (no other caller, no switch/type dependency), one bounded one-record head read, and it keeps a truncated Kernel file from yielding a seemingly valid empty terminal page. Restoring the DELETE block is forbidden by AGENTS.md rule 4 / decision 79-4. Note for the lead: TP-112's coverage sentence cites only :495-497 and claims the same check is covered by :849-853, but this occurrence is :470, whose only coverage was the deleted :897-904 block; that does not change the U ruling (no test needed), it only corrects the item's coverage note.
